title: Dangerous Goods: Plates & Basics
whatItIs: Vehicles carrying dangerous goods in packages show plain orange plates; tankers show hazard warning plates. Drivers need ADR training, and some tunnels ban certain loads.
keyFacts: Vehicles carrying dangerous goods in packages are marked with plain orange reflective plates.
Road tankers and vehicles carrying tank containers of dangerous goods have hazard warning plates.

keyFacts.text: Drivers carrying dangerous goods MUST hold an ADR training certificate, unless an exemption applies.

keyFacts: On ADR journeys, carry the transport documents, emergency instructions in writing and photo ID for each crew member.
Tunnel signs can ban dangerous goods by restriction code: Dartford is category C, Blackwall category E.

items.title: Follow rule 283
items.text: Stop safely, hazard lights on, call 999 with full details.

items.title: Engines off, no smoking
items.text: Switch off engines and DO NOT SMOKE.

items.title: Keep well away
items.text: Don't try to rescue casualties: you could become one yourself.

items.title: Report the markings
items.text: Tell the emergency services about the labels and markings on the vehicle.

b.label: Hazard warning plate
points: Shows a diamond symbol for the hazard

onTheTest.question: A lorry is displaying plain orange reflective plates. What does this tell you?
options: It's carrying dangerous goods in packages
It's a tanker carrying flammable liquid
onTheTest.why: Vehicles carrying dangerous goods in packages are marked with plain orange reflective plates. Tankers have hazard warning plates.

onTheTest.question: A tanker carrying dangerous goods has crashed. What should you tell the emergency services?
options: As much as you can about its labels and markings
Only the number of vehicles involved
Nothing until you have checked the load
Only the name of the haulier
onTheTest.why: Call the emergency services and give as much information as possible about the labels and markings on the vehicle.

traps: Don't use a mobile phone close to a vehicle carrying flammable loads.
Below certain amounts, many parts of ADR may not apply, or apply in a modified form: not none at all.
Emergency instructions must be in a language every crew member understands.
